No candidate matched a published URL. picks.rationale: Full-duplex voice - the model listening and backchanneling while you talk - is a genuinely new turn-taking pattern designers now have to spec, not just faster TTS.
picks.excerpt: GPT-Live's full-duplex architecture lets ChatGPT listen and speak at once, backchanneling 'mhmm' while you talk. Overlapping turn-taking is a genuinely new interaction pattern to design around, not just a faster TTS.

picks.rationale: A concrete audit you can run tomorrow: check dependencies against Baseline and strip 60-90KB of gzipped code that agents and templates keep bolting on for features browsers already ship.
picks.excerpt: Auditing dependencies against Baseline feature status can strip 60-90KB of gzipped code that browsers now handle natively. A concrete way to stop agents and templates from bolting on libraries the platform already replaced.

picks.rationale: A free 30-minute Gnomon workshop that argues hard-surface concepting belongs in a headset - VR sculpting into KeyShot finishing, a workflow shift you can try the same afternoon.
picks.excerpt: The Gnomon Workshop released a free 30-minute tutorial in which concept artist Andre-Lang Huynh designs a mech entirely inside VR with Substance 3D Modeler, then finishes in KeyShot. It is a concrete argument for sculpting hard-surface concepts in headset rather than on a mouse.

picks.rationale: Applies Stafford Beer's viable systems theory to AI products: the app is a feedback loop between user, model and interface, which changes what the designer is actually shaping.
picks.excerpt: Applying Stafford Beer's viable systems theory to AI-era products: the app is a feedback loop between user, model and interface rather than a stack of screens. It changes what the designer is actually shaping.

picks.rationale: Turns a live controversy into a habit change: keep sketches, drafts and version history, because process documentation is becoming the only proof a human made the work.
picks.excerpt: After Square Enix's AI accusation cycle, the argument is blunt: keeping your sketches, drafts and version history may soon be the only way to prove a human made the work. Process documentation becomes a professional defence, not housekeeping.
